messages.subject: Instructions to advise — Pennington v Crossfield (merits & quantum)
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Clerks,

We should be grateful if Ms Stanford could advise in writing on the merits and quantum of the proposed claim by Pennington Industries against Crossfield Engineering. Instructions, the supply agreement, the Wraysbury report and the pre-action correspondence will follow on the e-platform today. The key issue is the clause 11 limitation/exclusion. Could you let us know Ms Stanford's availability and fee estimate?

Kind regards,
James Osei

messages.subject: Counsel's advice received — Pennington v Crossfield
messages.plaintextBody:
Sarah, Grace,

Harriet Stanford's advice is in and attached. Headlines: liability prospects good (70–75%); causation defensible but needs a Part 35 metallurgist; the real exposure is clause 11. She thinks there are decent arguments that the £742k lost-production head is direct loss (outside 11.2) and that the £214,830 cap may be unreasonable under UCTA. Realistic recovery ranges from ~£215k (worst case) to £1.6–2.0m; sensible settlement value £1.1–1.4m.

She recommends we issue without delay, instruct an expert, and make an early Part 36 offer. Happy to talk it through.

James

--
Whitfield Carter LLP
22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
DX 138760 Cheapside | +44 (0)20 7946 0991
